description.value:
Qliph-Scarred. You walked out of a place that should have unmade you. The hollows and fractures in your soul never fully closed, and the world can feel the pressure leaking out.

Qliph-Scarred Traits

  • Creature Type. Humanoid (Qliph-Scarred).

  • Size. You are Medium.

  • Speed. Your walking speed is 6 squares

  • attributes. Your background determines your attribute increases; Qliph-Scarred does not grant any attribute bonuses.

Your Qliph-Scarred heritage grants you additional features through advancements (Item Grants) added during character creation.

description.value:
“Darkness climbed into your bones and decided to stay.”

Shadow Resilience. Your scars drink in hostile power instead of letting it tear you apart.

  • You have resistance to qliphothic damage.
  • Your presence carries a subtle, unsettling weight; you gain a small bonus to Intimidation checks.
  • The deeper interactions with corruption, Qliphothic zones, and Darkness tracks are handled by Bad Eden engines and GM judgment.

effects.name: Qliph-Scarred: Shadow Resilience
effects.description: You have resistance to necrotic damage and a +1 bonus to Intimidation checks. Any extra “corruption handling” stays narrative/BBTTCC-engine side, not automated rolls.

description.value:
Qliphothic Saturation. The hollows in you are already full of poison light.

  • You have resistance to poison damage.
  • You often sense when a place is spiritually “overclocked” or unsafe; your scars hum in high-corruption zones.
  • Any radiation/corruption hooks in Bad Eden are driven by flags on this feature rather than automatic rolls.

effects.name: Qliph-Scarred: Qliphothic Saturation (Resist Poison)
effects.description: You have resistance to poison damage. Advantage on saves vs the poisoned condition is adjudicated by the GM.

description.value:
Hunger Mask. You learned to wear your appetites like armor.

  • You gain a small bonus to Stealth checks when hiding fear, pain, or desire.
  • Your body handles starvation, deprivation, and toxic cravings slightly better than most (handled narratively).
  • In Qliphothic zones, your mask sometimes slips, revealing the hollow radiance beneath.

effects.name: Qliph-Scarred: Hunger Mask (Social Edge)
effects.description: You gain a +1 bonus to Deception checks when concealing your true intentions or emotional state.

description.value:
Shadow-Wake. Wherever you go, the shadows remember.

  • You leave behind subtle impressions in darkness and ruin; tracking you by mundane means is slightly harder.
  • You gain a small bonus to Stealth checks while in dim light or darkness.
  • Qliphothic entities may recognize the wake you leave, for better or worse (handled narratively).

effects.name: Qliph-Scarred: Shadow-Wake (Stealth Edge)
effects.description: You gain a +1 bonus to Stealth checks, especially when moving through dim light or deeper shadow.

description.value:
“Send the Qliph-Scarred into the bad places. If they come back smiling, it means the rest of probably can still come back.”

OP Edge. Your faction leans toward problem-solving in corrupted zones, containment operations, and subtle social pressure.

Corruption-Tuned. You help keep others steady in the presence of Darkness, even when it whispers to you first.

effects.name: Qliph-Scarred: Strategic Hooks (Bad Eden OP Flags)
effects.description: Data-only for your Bad Eden OP and world engines: Qliph-Scarred factions lean toward Intrigue and Non-Lethal lines, especially in corrupted or unstable zones.

description.value:
Bad Eden Heritage (v1.1, RFI-native). Qliph-Scarred heritage: Husk.

“What the void took, it didn’t replace. That’s the feature, not the bug.”

Qliph-Scarred (Husk). Your scar is a hollow. Something was removed from you in a place that should have unmade you, and it never got put back. People who try to read you feel the draft. Manifestations that look inside find less to grab. You walked out emptier, and in this world, emptier can mean harder to kill.

Traits

  • Creature Type. Humanoid (Qliph-Scarred).

  • Size. Medium.

  • Movement. 6 squares walking.

  • Lineage Lean. Qliph-Scarred does not grant fixed attribute bonuses; your background handles increases. Your heritage leans toward Mind in fiction and through Tier powers.

Qliph-Scarred Core: What Walked Out

Shared across all Qliph-Scarred heritages. Granted at character creation via the base ancestry item.

  • Shadow Resilience. You have resistance to qliphothic damage. You reroll the lowest die on Body checks against effects that would drain, wither, or corrupt your body.

  • Qliphothic Saturation. Once per scene, when you fail a Soul check, you may reroll it — but your scene's Darkness-gain count increases by 1. The scar pays for what the scar saves.

  • Hunger Mask. You can suppress a bodily need (hunger, thirst, sleep, breath) for up to 24 hours by deciding to; you do not suffer its penalties during that window. At the end of the 24 hours, all deferred needs strike you at once, each as a separate Stress-class consequence.

  • Shadow-Wake. Creatures with qliphothic attunement (demons, corrupt sephirot, Radiation-warped entities) can sense you at 12 squares and know you have been marked. They may not know how to read the mark.

Husk Traits

  • Hollow Core. You have resistance to psychic damage. Creatures attempting to read your thoughts, detect your lies, or determine your emotional state do so at disadvantage. Divination-register effects that would reveal information about you have a 50% chance to return nothing — just the hollow echo of the question.

  • No Weight Inside. You do not need to eat or drink, though you still may. The void is not demanding, once you learn to carry it.

Strategic Hooks (Foundry / Bad Eden)

  • OP Edge. Your faction gains +2 Intrigue OP and +1 Non-Lethal OP at campaign start.

  • Hex Synergy. In Empty / Abandoned / Liminal hexes, your faction's infiltration and passage operations cost 1 fewer OP.

  • Nothing to Grab. Once per Strategic Turn, when a rival faction attempts a divination, intelligence, or surveillance operation targeting your faction, you may force them to reroll that check. They find less than they expected.

description.value:
"They looked for you in all the usual places. None of them were the right shape."

The Quiet Inside (1/Soma Break). Reaction — when you are targeted by a divination, mind-reading, or truth-detection effect, force the caster to roll their effect against your Resolve instead of its normal save DC.

Failure: the effect returns nothing — no partial information, no awareness that a target was present.

Success: you take 1 point of Stress from the pressure of the probe.

When divination / mind-read / truth-detect targets you, force caster to roll vs your Resolve. Fail → effect returns nothing, no detection. Success → 1 Stress.

⚙ ENGINE NOTE — Pace is now ◆ Surge. Movement banks Surge (capped per round); your courier moves are the ◆ Surge menu's courier kit (Courier's Step / Ghoststep / Flank & Strike / No Such Door + your route's kit). Read Pace as Surge wherever it appears below.

"You're already moving. The fight rearranges around it."

The Shadow Courier runs on Surge, like everyone — but yours comes from motion. Move 30+ ft in a turn and you bank +1 Surge (again at 12 squares, max +2/round). A courier in motion has options; a courier standing still is just a target. The old Pace pool folds into this — same fuel, one number.

The Courier (spent via Surge)

  • Courier's Step (1) — +half-speed move (no provoke) and a freed reaction; flow through the fight.
  • Ghoststep (3) — DR equal to Tier till your next turn, and reposition out of danger.
  • Flank & Strike (5) — reposition, then your next Strike reroll the lowest die and +Tier d6.
  • No Such Door (8) — allies within Tier squares each gain a freed reaction and a reroll; open the road for the whole team.

The Package endures as your work — designate it, carry it, deliver it. Delivery banks your Surge to full and still triggers the route's strategic payoff (Intrigue OP, Darkness reduction, the arrival that mattered).

items.name: Last Mile L1: The Weight You Carry

system.source: Bad Eden Bulwark + Shadow Courier v1.0 (RFI-native rules)

description.value:
Nobody stays behind.

Mode: Psychopomp / drift: Sideways.

Your default Package type is a Soul — a specific character, creature, or intangible (a secret, a confession, a deathbed wish, a refugee's name, an unfinished obligation) that cannot reach safety on its own.

While carrying a Soul:

  • Your movement speed is reduced by 1 square, but allies traveling with you gain +1 square of movement speed (the Soul's witness-weight pulls them forward).

  • You reroll the lowest die on Stealth (Intrigue) and Athletics (Violence) checks made specifically to protect or conceal the Soul (not all stealth/athletics — just protective acts).

On delivery: When you successfully deliver a Soul to safety (the GM confirms the destination counts as safety for that Soul), the recipient faction gains +1 Morale OP and Darkness in the recipient's hex is reduced by 1 point.

You may receive a new Soul any time your Package slot is empty.

system.requirements: Route of the Last Mile, Shadow Courier Initiation 1

⚙ ENGINE NOTE — Pace is now ◆ Surge. Movement banks Surge (capped per round); your courier moves are the ◆ Surge menu's courier kit (Courier's Step / Ghoststep / Flank & Strike / No Such Door + your route's kit). Read Pace as Surge wherever it appears below.

You cross what isn't supposed to be crossed — and you always come out the other side carrying something.

On gaining Shadow Courier Initiation 1 you receive:

  • Skill rank +1 in Stealth (Intrigue).

  • Skill rank +1 in Tinkering (Intrigue).

  • Intrigue OP cap +2 and Logistics OP cap +2 on the faction your character belongs to.

  • Pace pool comes online (movement-generated). Max = max(2, ceil((Intrigue value + Shadow Courier Initiation) / 3)), capped at 8. Refills on Soma Break and on Package delivery.

  • Package slot comes online — one Package at a time, type set by your chosen Route at L1.

Pace generation. Gain 1 Pace when you move at least 6 squares on your turn. Maximum 1 Pace generated per turn from this feature. Doctrine features may add their own generators.

Baseline Pace spends (free action, 1 Pace each):

  • Move 5 extra feet without spending an action.

  • Reroll a single Stealth (Intrigue), Athletics (Violence), or Tinkering (Intrigue) check — keep the new result.

  • Ignore a single reaction strike against you on this turn.

Liminal Sense. Once per encounter, ignore the first detection-style roll an opponent attempts against you (perception, scrying, Insight to read your intent, etc.). The roll is treated as if it had failed; resources spent on the attempt are not refunded.

items.name: Route of the Last Mile (Bad Eden)

system.source: Bad Eden Originals — Sprint F (2026 rules)

description.value:
"Give it to me. I carry things."

Doctrine: Carry the unbearable thing to where it must go — intimate, burdensome, exact. Who bears the package now?

The Last Mile is the courier as the one who refuses to let it fall. Your Surge spends take the weight off others: shoulder their wounds at your own cost, carry an ally through a place that should have killed them, and deliver the unbearable thing intact.

Route (spent via Surge)

  • Shoulder the Weight (1) — heal an ally Tier d6; you take half as Stress; they bank a reroll.
  • Quiet Voyage (2) — an ally gains DR equal to Tier, and the next hit that would drop them is held at 1.
  • Delivered (5) — restore a fallen or badly-hurt ally to half Integrity and clear a condition.

“This must end for something else to begin.”

Archetype (Bad Eden): Death (Transformer). You are not annihilation. You are necessary ending, painful transition, and the force that cuts dead things loose so the living can survive.

Archetype Effects

  • Faction Edge. Your archetype strengthens sacrifice, transition, and value recovered from collapse. This Archetype is associated with +1 Violence and +1 Culture in faction calculus.
  • Tier Engine. See this Archetype’s Tier feats (Tier 1–4) for your full tactical and strategic toolkit.

attributes (Archetype ASI)

Common patterns include:

  • Merciless Midwife: +2 Soul, +1 Violence
  • Ruin-Reader: +2 Mind, +1 Soul
  • Breaker of Cycles: +1 Violence, +1 Soul, +1 Body

description.value:
Crew Type (Bad Eden): Ashbound Survivors.

“You don’t conquer the wasteland. You outlast it.”

Ashbound Survivors know how to live where maps stop pretending. They ration breath, read heat shimmer like scripture, and treat hostile terrain as a negotiation instead of a death sentence.

  • Tactical Identity: You gain a skill rank in Athletics and Lore.
  • Strategic Identity: Your faction starts with +1 Economy OPs.

Judgment - Necessary force. +1 Violence, +1 Logistics OPs

Geburah draws the line. It rewards discipline, enforcement, and decisive action against fortified problems, but always risks becoming cruelty if severity outruns wisdom.

Occult Association (Bad Eden): Shaman.

“You don’t fix the world. You listen to what it’s trying to become.”

Shamans do not impose order. They enter into relationship.

To a Shaman, the Great Work is not about forcing alignment onto a dead world. It is about hearing the pulse that is still there and deciding whether to protect it, guide it, or stand aside long enough for it to speak clearly. Every Hex is alive in some way. Every leyline has mood. Every storm is making a decision. Every spirit remembers who treated the land like a partner and who treated it like inventory.

Where Kabbalists map structure and Alchemists force conversion, Shamans work by attunement. They negotiate with terrain, weather, spirits, and flow-states that existed before factions learned to count OP.

How Shamans pursue the Great Work:

  • By listening to terrain, weather, and spirit pressure
  • By stabilizing living systems instead of extracting from them
  • By redirecting corruption rather than merely containing it
  • By treating Hexes as relationships, not assets

Resonance: Netzach / Living Flow — endurance, ecology, instinctive continuity, and the intelligence of systems nobody designed.

Tell-tales: mud where there should not be mud, animals that stop running, weather that feels briefly conversational.

Faction Effect (Passive):

  • +1 specialty edge on relevant terrain, travel, weather, or wilderness-facing OP rolls (GM adjudicates the exact OP lane)

Cost Principle: attunement creates obligation. The more the land speaks to you, the less you can pretend not to hear it. Expect spirit attention, place-based duty, and backlash when your faction acts against the needs of a living Hex.

Tier 1 (Level 1) — Death (Transformer)

  • Tactical: You gain a skill rank in Faith and Intimidation.
  • Strategic: Your faction's passive OP bias now follows the base Archetype file.

Tier 1 — Ashbound Survivors

You’ve learned the first mercy of dead land: preparation beats optimism.

  • Tactical: You gain a skill rank in Athletics and Lore.
  • Strategic: In Desert, Ash Wastes, and Wasteland hexes, environmental travel penalties are reduced and hazard pressure is easier to withstand.

Tier 1 — Shaman

“It was talking before. You just couldn’t hear it yet.”

At Tier 1, you become perceptible to the world and the world becomes perceptible to you.

You can feel when a place is hungry, when a storm is about to turn mean, and when a Hex is carrying more pressure than its surface suggests. You are not commanding Lore yet. You are learning its tone.

Tactical (Character Scale)

  • Gain a skill rank in Lore and Athletics
  • You can perform a brief attunement to sense whether a nearby area is spiritually calm, distressed, corrupted, or unusually resonant

Strategic (Faction Scale)

  • Hex Attunement: upon entering a new Hex, you learn one of the following about it: dominant flow-state, unusual weather pressure, leyline disturbance, or corruption presence
  • Once per Strategic Turn, gain +1 to one relevant travel, terrain, or wilderness-facing OP roll

Cost: once the world starts speaking to you, silence gets rare. Expect distraction, omen pressure, or spirit agitation when your faction ignores what a place is telling you.

item.lore:
Standard-issue field knife. Single-edge, thumb groove, hard sheath that clips to a belt or boot. The first weapon most Stewards carry and the last one they put down. Honest steel — no signature, no story, just edge.

Standard Issue. Light enough for off-hand work; close enough for the kind of conversation knives are for.
